title: Where TLS ends
claim: Where TLS ends decides whether the load balancer sees the request and whether the last hop is encrypted.
alt: Three panels. In the first, the client sends HTTPS to an Application Load Balancer, which sends plain HTTP to the instance. In the second, the load balancer sends HTTPS to the instance. In the third, a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener passes the encrypted traffic to the instance, which decrypts it.
notes: Brief 14; 2-deep.md#encryption-to-the-targets-needs-a-second-tls-connection-or-a-pass-through, after the trace; caption, no steps. Title, claim, alt from brief.json. Same structure in every panel, drawn top to bottom so the three panels fit one desktop row; only the last hop and the load balancer type change.
